records.text:
Accumulation of a finely granular basophilic material within the follicular and sebaceous gland epithelium. A moderate perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of lymphocytes, lacking cytological atypia, was observed in the superficial and mid dermis. No epidermotropism nor vacuolar degeneration of the basal layer. Alcian blue stain demonstrated the presence of mucin.
Multiple skin-colored and erythematous follicular papules coalescing into a linear plaque involving the patient's forehead, as well as the dorsum and tip of the nose (A). Two skin punch biopsies from the forehead and nose (B and C).

records.query: Need the dermoscopic description of the facial lesions and T-cell receptor gene rearrangement results to differentiate benign follicular mucinosis from early mycosis fungoides, which is critical for confirming a benign nevoid/segmental lesion versus a chronic inflammatory dermatosis.

Need the T-cell receptor gene rearrangement study results from the skin biopsy specimen, as this molecular test is the critical next step to confirm polyclonal (reactive) versus clonal T-cell population, thereby distinguishing benign follicular mucinosis from early mycosis fungoides and firmly validating the chronic inflammatory dermatosis diagnosis.

bindings.label: Slightly pruritic lesions on the face for 1 year
Patient is a girl younger than 2 years, born after an uncomplicated pregnancy and delivery, with growth and development appropriate for age
No associated symptoms such as fever, anorexia, or weight loss were noted

Physical examination revealed multiple skin-colored and erythematous follicular papules (1-2 mm) in a segmental pattern on the right forehead, dorsum and tip of nose; a small excoriated plaque on the right malar area; no mucosal lesions; rest of examination unremarkable
Skin biopsy histopathology shows follicular and sebaceous epithelial mucin deposition with Alcian blue positivity, mild lymphocytic infiltrate, and no cytological atypia or epidermotropism
The facial lesion is follicular mucinosis
T-cell receptor gene rearrangement results are pending/not yet available
Early mycosis fungoides (cutaneous T-cell lymphoma) presenting as follicular mucinosis
Positron emission tomography showed increased uptake in the left adrenal gland with a standardized uptake value of 7.4
